Resident remittances hit $2.74 billion i.takeaway: Monthly outflows were $2.74 billion in August 2026; the long history includes changes in what LRS reports.
Resident remittances hit $2.74 billion i.detail: The record covers 221 calendar months from April 2008 to August 2026. The June and September 2023 peaks preceded the announced TCS deadlines, but their timing alone does not measure the tax effect.
Resident remittances hit $2.74 billion i.whyShowThis: Shows the full monthly history, including abrupt changes hidden by annual totals.
Resident remittances hit $2.74 billion i.howToRead: The top line is total monthly LRS in USD millions. The comparison lines group travel and studies abroad, family maintenance with gifts and donations, and deposits with property and equity/debt.
Resident remittances hit $2.74 billion i.mistakeToAvoid: The reporting boundary expanded in 2015. These groups also omit the small medical-treatment and other lines, so they are not an exhaustive decomposition.
Resident remittances hit $2.74 billion i.mobileNote: Read the total alongside its purpose groups; a rise in travel is different from a rise in asset purchases.

Resident LRS outflows were $29 billion i.takeaway: The remittance window is one part of cross-border flows, with different populations behind each measure.
Resident LRS outflows were $29 billion i.detail: Resident LRS outflows were $28.98 billion in FY2025-26. Gross inward private transfers were $155.12 billion and gross outward FDI debits were $37.33 billion. Private transfers are broader than household remittances; FDI includes investors beyond resident individuals.
Resident LRS outflows were $29 billion i.whyShowThis: Provides a compact scale comparison before examining the purposes and rules within LRS.
Resident LRS outflows were $29 billion i.howToRead: All bars show gross flows in USD billions during the same fiscal year. Their different coverage means they cannot be summed or treated as offsets.
Resident LRS outflows were $29 billion i.mistakeToAvoid: LRS can overlap the investment figures. A larger inward flow does not establish that a particular outward payment has no effect on the external balance.
Resident LRS outflows were $29 billion i.mobileNote: Read the labels and gross-flow definitions before comparing lengths.

Education and other travel account for 9.takeaway: Education and other travel made up 97.6% of the March-August 2026 travel total; business and pilgrimage were 2.1%.
Education and other travel account for 9.detail: The frozen source reports $7,995.32 million across these six months. Education travel was $3,322.07 million and other travel $4,478.90 million; the residual label does not identify holidays or credit-card spending separately.
Education and other travel account for 9.whyShowThis: Measures the categories named in press reports of a possible travel sub-limit.
Education and other travel account for 9.howToRead: Each row is one month; the columns show the five travel categories in USD millions.
Education and other travel account for 9.mistakeToAvoid: Category spending is not the amount a per-person ceiling would save. The source contains no distribution of remittances per person.
Education and other travel account for 9.mobileNote: Compare the education and other-travel columns with the much smaller business and pilgrimage columns.

Two education-related LRS lines totalled.takeaway: The two education-related lines totalled $1,047.36 million in August 2026, or 38.2% of LRS that month.
Two education-related LRS lines totalled.detail: Studies Abroad was $191.84 million and Travel for education was $855.52 million. Combining them gives a broader observable measure than either line alone, without proving why the older studies line declined.
Two education-related LRS lines totalled.whyShowThis: Prevents a single reporting category from being mistaken for all education-related remittances.
Two education-related LRS lines totalled.howToRead: The studies line has a longer history. Education travel and the combined line begin only in March 2026, when both components are observable.
Two education-related LRS lines totalled.mistakeToAvoid: Missing earlier education-travel observations are not zero. Do not calculate combined growth across that missing-data boundary.
Two education-related LRS lines totalled.mobileNote: The latest combined point is the sum of the two components, not an additional outflow.

Capital transfers added $1.03 billion wh.takeaway: The capital-transfer increase was larger than the increase in total LRS, with declines in the remaining purposes offsetting part of it.
Capital transfers added $1.03 billion wh.detail: Across matched April-August windows, capital transfers increased by $1.03 billion while the remaining purposes combined fell by about $491 million. Total LRS increased by about $538 million. The chart groups main purposes so each payment enters the accounting once.
Capital transfers added $1.03 billion wh.whyShowThis: Explains the change in the headline rather than presenting separate growth rates with no reconciliation.
Capital transfers added $1.03 billion wh.howToRead: Bars to the right add to the change in total LRS; bars to the left offset it. Values are changes in USD millions, not the level of each purpose.
Capital transfers added $1.03 billion wh.mistakeToAvoid: Travel and studies are combined across the reporting change. This does not identify education demand, investor motives or a causal tax effect.
Capital transfers added $1.03 billion wh.mobileNote: Start with the capital-transfer bar, then read the offsetting travel-and-studies bar.

Resident investment in foreign equities,.takeaway: Deposits, property and equity/debt totalled $3,933.79 million in FY2025-26, against $1,141.21 million in FY2019-20.
Resident investment in foreign equities,.detail: Equity/debt contributed $2,652.01 million in the latest fiscal year. The aggregate lines do not identify whether individual remitters moved from deposits into securities, or whether investment used an IFSC account.
Resident investment in foreign equities,.whyShowThis: Shows how the composition of personal overseas asset remittances changed over the longer record.
Resident investment in foreign equities,.howToRead: The three lines show April-March fiscal-year totals in USD millions; the axis names the ending year.
Resident investment in foreign equities,.mistakeToAvoid: The lines record outward remittances, not the stock of overseas wealth, investment returns or net capital flight.
Resident investment in foreign equities,.mobileNote: Read equity/debt separately from deposits and property.

March takes an outsized share of annual.takeaway: March receives about 17% of annual capital transfers on average; August receives about 14% of the direct studies line.
March takes an outsized share of annual.detail: Each month is divided by the same channel’s full-year remittances before averaging across FY2022-23 to FY2025-26. This gives each complete financial year equal weight and excludes the partial latest year.
March takes an outsized share of annual.whyShowThis: Tests the calendar pattern without letting larger years dominate the comparison.
March takes an outsized share of annual.howToRead: Compare months within each channel. Each channel has its own annual denominator, and its twelve average monthly shares add to about 100%.
March takes an outsized share of annual.mistakeToAvoid: These are unweighted averages of within-year shares, not pooled monthly dollar totals. The direct studies line does not measure all education spending, and timing does not establish a remitter’s motive.
March takes an outsized share of annual.mobileNote: Use the month labels to compare March capital transfers and August direct studies.

After the TCS changes, family transfers.takeaway: Family maintenance was lower in the later policy window, while travel and equity/debt were higher.
After the TCS changes, family transfers.detail: Monthly maintenance averaged $347.8 million in FY2022-23 and $294.3 million in April 2025-August 2026. Equity/debt rose from $104.7 million to $257.5 million and travel from $1,138.5 million to $1,372.9 million across those windows.
After the TCS changes, family transfers.whyShowThis: Compares the observed flows around changes in TCS without assigning the whole change to the tax.
After the TCS changes, family transfers.howToRead: Each column is an unequal-length policy window. Compare monthly averages, in USD millions per month, within a purpose row.
After the TCS changes, family transfers.mistakeToAvoid: This is not a causal tax experiment. Education and medical remittances have different TCS treatment; TCS credits can still tie up cash until offset or refunded.
After the TCS changes, family transfers.mobileNote: Read the two endpoint columns first, then the pre-deadline period.

Rupee depreciation quietly expanded the.takeaway: The rupee equivalent of $250,000 rose from Rs 159.13 lakh in June 2015 to Rs 237.95 lakh in August 2026.
Rupee depreciation quietly expanded the.detail: The illustration uses the implied valuation rate obtained by dividing RBI reserve values in INR by USD values. The increase was Rs 78.82 lakh, or 49.5%; it is not a measure of affordability relative to incomes.
Rupee depreciation quietly expanded the.whyShowThis: Shows how a fixed foreign-currency limit changes in domestic-currency terms.
Rupee depreciation quietly expanded the.howToRead: The main line is the ceiling's rupee equivalent. The reported Rs 50 lakh proposal is a contextual benchmark, not a historical rule; the TCS threshold starts only in October 2020.
Rupee depreciation quietly expanded the.mistakeToAvoid: The implied reserve valuation rate is not a bank's retail exchange quote. No remitter counts show how many people approach the ceiling.
Rupee depreciation quietly expanded the.mobileNote: Compare the main line's endpoints; the proposal benchmark has no historical effective date.
